sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: create_specifier_set
tools.description:
Create a SpecifierSet object from a string or iterable of specifiers to represent version constraints.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of a specifier or a comma-separated list of specifiers
        prereleases (bool, optional): Whether to accept prerelease versions if applicable
    
    Returns:
        str: String representation of the SpecifierSet object
    
    Example:
        >>> create_specifier_set(">=3.0,!=3.1")
        '<SpecifierSet object>'

tools.name: create_version
tools.description: Parse and create a Version object from a version string for comparison and manipulation. version_string: A string representation of a version conforming to PEP 440, e.g. '1.0a5' -> '<Version('1.0a5')>'.

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a SpecifierSet into a VersionRange string representation. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: specifier_set_contains_version
tools.description: Check if a specific version is contained within this SpecifierSet. specifier_set: A string representation of the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check for containment in the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.

tools.name: is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether a specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    A specifier set is unsatisfiable if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously
        
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_subset
tools.description:
Check if every version matching this set also matches another given set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: A string representation of the first specifier set
        other_set: A string representation of the second specifier set to check against
    
    Returns:
        True if every version matching the first set also matches the second set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_subset(">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_superset
tools.description:
Return whether every version matching other also matches this set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the main specifier set
        other_set (str): A string representation of the other specifier set to check against
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if every version matching other also matches this set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: are_specifier_sets_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two SpecifierSets share no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set1 (string): First specifier set string
        specifier_set2 (string): Second specifier set string
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets share no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> are_specifier_sets_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description:
Return a VersionRange that includes all possible PEP 440 versions.
    
    Args:
        admit_arbitrary: Whether to admit arbitrary version strings, not just valid PEP 440 versions
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; None means use default behavior
    
    Returns:
        String representation of the full VersionRange
    
    Example:
        >>> create_full_version_range()
        'VersionRange(full=True)'

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Return a VersionRange that contains no versions. prereleases: whether pre-release versions should be considered.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Create a VersionRange that contains only a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string or Version object, e.g. '1.0' -> VersionRange singleton for 1.0. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; if None, uses the default behavior.

tools.name: filter_versions_by_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range.
    
    Args:
        version_range_spec: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        iterable: An iterable of version strings
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
    
    Example:
        >>> filter_versions_by_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: range_contains_version
tools.description: Check if a specific version is contained within this VersionRange. specifier_set: A specifier set that can be converted to a VersionRange using .to_range(). version: The version string to check for containment in the range. >>> range_contains_version('>=1.0,<2.0', '1.5') True >>> range_contains_version('>=1.0,<2.0', '2.0') False

tools.name: is_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if every version in range1 is also in range2. range1: A version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.5,<1.8' -> True. range2: Another version range specifier string to check if range1 is a subset of this.

tools.name: is_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if every version in another range is also in this range. range1: A version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Another version range specifier string to check if it's a subset of range1. Example: is_version_range_superset('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<1.8') -> True.

tools.name: are_version_ranges_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two version ranges share no common versions.
    
    Args:
        version_range1 (str): A version range specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        version_range2 (str): Another version range specifier string (e.g., '>=2.0,<3.0')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the ranges are disjoint (share no common versions), False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> are_version_ranges_disjoint('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0')
        True

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description:
Combine two version ranges into one that includes all versions from either range.
    
    Both operands must share the same configured pre-release policy; otherwise ValueError is raised.
    
    Args:
        version_range_a (str): First version range in PEP 440 format
        version_range_b (str): Second version range in PEP 440 format
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the combined version range
        
    Example:
        >>> union_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<3.0")
        '>=1.0,<3.0'

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description:
Create a VersionRange that includes only versions present in both input ranges.
    
    Args:
        range1 (str): First version range specifier
        range2 (str): Second version range specifier
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the intersected version range
    
    Example:
        >>> intersect_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description:
Create a VersionRange that includes versions in the first range but not in the second.
    
    Args:
        first_range (string): A version specifier string representing the first version range
        second_range (string): A version specifier string representing the second version range to exclude
    
    Returns:
        string: A version specifier string representing the difference range
    
    Example:
        >>> difference_version_ranges(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: is_version_prerelease
tools.description: Check if a version string represents a pre-release version. version: a version string, e.g. '1.2.3a1' -> true.

tools.name: get_version_release
tools.description: Get the release components of a Version object as a tuple. version: A version string to parse and extract the release components from e.g. '1.2.3' -> (1, 2, 3).

tools.name: get_version_pre
tools.description: Get the pre-release segment of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the pre-release segment from -> The pre-release segment as a tuple of (letter, number) or None if no pre-release segment exists.

tools.name: get_version_post
tools.description:
Get the post-release number of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release number from
    
    >>> print(Version("1.2.3").post)
    None
    >>> Version("1.2.3.post1").post
    1

tools.name: get_version_dev
tools.description: Get the development number of a Version object. version: A version string compatible with packaging.version.Version -> The development number of the version, or None if not a development version.

tools.name: get_version_local
tools.description:
Get the local version segment of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the local version segment from
    
    >>> print(Version("1.2.3").local)
    None
    >>> Version("1.2.3+abc").local
    'abc'

tools.name: is_version_postrelease
tools.description: Check if a version string represents a post-release version. version: a version string, e.g. '1.2.3.post1' -> true.

tools.name: is_version_devrelease
tools.description: Check if a version string represents a development release. version: a version string, e.g. '1.2.3.dev1' -> true.

tools.name: get_version_major
tools.description:
Get the major version component of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the major version from -> The first item of release or 0 if unavailable.
    
    >>> get_version_major("1.2.3")
    1

tools.name: get_version_minor
tools.description: Get the minor version component of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the minor version from -> The second item of release or 0 if unavailable.

tools.name: get_version_micro
tools.description: Get the micro version component of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the micro version from -> The third item of release or 0 if unavailable.

tools.name: get_version_epoch
tools.description: Get the epoch of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the epoch from -> int

tools.name: get_version_public
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version string. version: a version string, e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: get_version_base
tools.description: Get the base version of a Version object. version: A version string to parse and extract the base version from -> The base version string without pre or post release markers.

tools.name: canonicalize_version_string
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Normalize a Python package name to its canonical form. name: The name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name('Django') 'django'

tools.name: is_package_name_normalized
tools.description: Check if a package name is in its normalized form. name: The package name to check for normalization -> true if normalized, false otherwise.

tools.name: parse_version_string
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the Version constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version_string('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: create_specifier
tools.description: Create a Specifier object from a version specifier string. spec: A version specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0.0' -> Specifier object serialized as string. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: specifier_contains_version
tools.description:
Check if a specific version is contained within this Specifier.
    
    Args:
        specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'
        version: The version string to check for containment
        prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. 
                     If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.
    
    Returns:
        True if the version is contained in the specifier, False otherwise.
        
    Example:
        >>> specifier_contains_version('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: get_specifier_operator
tools.description: Get the operator part of a Specifier object. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '==1.2.3' -> '=='.

tools.name: get_specifier_version
tools.description: Get the version part of a Specifier object. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '==1.2.3' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: create_marker
tools.description: Create a Marker object from a dependency marker expression string. marker: The string representation of a marker expression, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> "<Marker('python_version >= "3.6"')>".

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description:
Evaluate a marker expression against an environment to determine if it's true.
    
    Args:
        marker: A marker expression to evaluate
        environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment
        context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid.
                 Accepted values are "metadata" (for core metadata; default), "lock_file", and "requirement".
    
    Returns:
        True if the marker matches, otherwise False
    
    Example:
        >>> evaluate_marker('python_version >= "3.6"', {"python_version": "3.8"})
        True
